Ip and Bt both along +phi (bp_sign=-1, bt_sign=1), so B_Z<0 at the outboard midplane and the electron diamagnetic direction is -phi (counter-current). Lab frame (pot0 Doppler <= ~10 kHz, negligible): NT propagates in the ELECTRON direction at psi_N 0.45-0.75 (-20 to -40 kHz for n=4-8, >85% phase coherence), weak ion direction (<10 kHz) at psi_N<0.45 and mixed outside 0.75; PT propagates in the electron direction over psi_N 0.35-0.85 (-5 to -10 kHz, coherence up to 0.98 for n=4) and in the ion direction at psi_N 0.85-0.95 (+8 kHz). Both runs are still in the linear/early-nonlinear phase at the end (NT dpot rms 4 V at 275 us, PT 0.2 V at 283 us; growth ~2e4/s). Real frequencies are far below the local omega_* estimates (50-500 kHz). Follow-up 2026-10-06: the electron-direction result is NOT an E x B Doppler artifact. From the full axisymmetric potential (pot0 and pot0m, late-time mean) E_R is within +-2.3 kV/m in NT, giving n*omega_E <= 11 kHz for n=8 and pointing in the ION direction at psi_N 0.50-0.70 (so the E x B-frame frequency is even more electron-directed, ~-40 kHz); in PT pot0 is ~0.03 V, no Doppler at all. Both runs are still linear (e*dpot/Te ~ 0.4% NT, 0.02% PT), so zonal flows are weak. Sign chain re-verified: XGC's get_ExB_drift (push_physics.tpp) is right-handed in (R,phi,Z), so with the stored B_Z<0 an adiabatic-electron drift wave propagates toward -phi; -phi = electron direction is therefore the code's own convention, not an assumption. Profiles (XGC_inputs/*_tcv69271_t1.1_NT.prf, *_tcv69508_t1.1_PT.prf) at psi_N 0.5-0.65: NT R/Ln 6-10, R/LTi 11-18, eta_i 1.8-1.9, Te/Ti 0.9, k_theta*rho_s(n=8) 0.22, f*e(n=8) 45-70 kHz -> measured -26..-29 kHz ~ 0.5 f*e; PT R/Ln 6-8, R/LTi 7-9, eta_i 1.2-1.5, Te/Ti 0.7-0.8, f*e 33-37 kHz -> measured -7..-10 kHz. Interpretation: near-marginal ITG (gamma ~2e4/s) in a peaked-density regime (epsilon_n = 2Ln/R ~ 0.2-0.33, close to the fluid-model sign-reversal threshold), where the ITG real frequency can sit in the electron direction.
